describe_webservice.title: Describe the web service's input and output schema
describe_webservice.description: Read the schema of the Businesslogic web service the API token belongs to (each token is bound to one published Excel model). Returns the service `name` and `version`, `expected_input` (a JSON Schema draft-07 object whose `properties` give each input's title, description, type, default, minimum/maximum/multipleOf and allowed `oneOf` values, plus `required` and `order`), `expected_output` (JSON Schema of the calculated fields) and `available_data` (lookup tables that inputs with `data_mapping_id` reference, e.g. id/label pairs). Call this first to learn which keys and values to send to execute_webservice.

output.description: The service descriptor: name, version, expected_input and expected_output JSON Schemas, and available_data lookup tables.

version.description: The published version of the model.

expected_input.description: JSON Schema (draft-07) of the input parameters /execute accepts.

expected_output.description: JSON Schema of the output parameters /execute returns.

available_data.description: Named lookup tables (arrays of id/label rows) referenced by inputs' data_mapping_id.

execute_webservice.title: Run the web service's Excel model with inputs
execute_webservice.description: Run the Excel model behind the Businesslogic web service the token belongs to: send the input values as a flat JSON object keyed by the input parameter names from describe_webservice (`expected_input.properties`), and get back the calculated outputs as a JSON object keyed by the output names in `expected_output` (e.g. {"total_amount": 40660}). If inputs are missing or invalid the service returns an array of validation entries with `field_path` and `error_strings` instead (e.g. "$.start_year: is missing but it is required"); call describe_webservice to check the names, types, bounds and allowed values first. Execution is a stateless calculation and does not modify the model.

inputs.description: The input parameter values, keyed by the property names from describe_webservice's expected_input schema, e.g. {"salary_per_month": 30000, "start_year": 100}. Values for inputs that use a lookup table (data_mapping_id) are the row ids from available_data, not the labels.

output.description: The calculated output values keyed by output parameter name, or an array of validation errors (field_path, error_strings, errors) when the inputs fail the schema.
